description.text: Adamo Tadolini was born on 21 December 1788 in Bologna into a family of sculptors, the grandson of Petronio Tadolini. He studied at the Accademia di Belle Arti in Bologna from 1808 to 1813 under Giacomo De Maria, winning a prize for a terracotta relief of Venus and Aeneas that earned him a scholarship to Rome.

In Rome he worked in the studio of the neo‑classical master Antonio Canova, producing a plaster statue of Ajax cursing the Gods. Canova helped him establish his own studio at Via Del Babuino 150 in 1822, a site that later became the Canova‑Tadolini Museum. Tadolini’s career included a range of public monuments, from the marble statue of St. Paul in St. Peter’s Square to a bronze equestrian statue of Simón Bolívar in Lima’s Plaza Bolívar.

curiosities.text: Tadolini’s studio at Via Del Babuino 150 is now a museum that houses a treasury of his and his family’s works.
His sons Scipione and Tito collaborated with him; after his death Scipione took ownership of the studio, which later passed to Giulio and Enrico Tadolini.
Among his most celebrated works is the bronze equestrian statue of Simón Bolívar, erected in the 1850s in Lima’s Plaza Bolívar and later replicated in Caracas.
